:::{#def-fitting-procedure}
#### Fitting procedure

A **fitting procedure** is a rule $\fitproc$ that,
given any data $\paren{(\predvar_{\iobs}, \outvar_{\iobs})}_{\iobs \in \obsidx}$ and any covariate value $\predvar$,
computes a [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) of the outcome at $\predvar$:

$$
\paren{\predvar; \paren{(\predvar_{\iobs}, \outvar_{\iobs})}_{\iobs \in \obsidx}}
\mapsto
\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \paren{(\predvar_{\iobs}, \outvar_{\iobs})}_{\iobs \in \obsidx}}.
$$ {#eq-fitting-procedure}

It is specified by these inputs:

- the data it is fitted to, which is not the covariate value $\predvar$ it predicts at;
- the set of candidate models it searches, called the model family;
- the objective function that scores each candidate against the data;
- the optimization algorithm that searches the family for a candidate with a good score, with its starting values and stopping rule;
- the random seed, when the algorithm draws random numbers, as in splitting the data;
- the [tuning parameters](#def-tuning-parameter), which it does not compute from the data;
- the preprocessing of the covariates, such as scaling, encoding and feature choice.

:::
